verdict.rationale: Railway's own marketing claims you can connect an existing repo with auto-config and 'no new tools to learn', and it ties into the Git pull-request workflow with per-PR previews; YAML config is optional. However, the evidence only covers the Git side of the story and is all first-party marketing, with nothing hands-on. missing for 10: documented integration with existing CI pipelines, any evidence about editor workflows, explicit framework-compatibility documentation, and independent corroboration that no proprietary tooling (e.g., the Railway CLI) is required.

support.subject: As a developer, I can keep using my existing Git, CI, editor, and framework workflows without adopting proprietary tooling

citations.quote: Connect your repo, Railway handles the rest. Auto-config, instant previews, no new tools to learn.
Every pull request gets its own preview. No surprises after merge.
Modify settings directly from the canvas. YAML optional.
